# QS-PROC-05 Machining surface finish (P1)
Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HT03

Scope
This quality specification defines the surface finish acceptance criteria, inspection method, and nonconformance handling for machined forgings produced on line P1-L4 and processed through the Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03). It applies to all incoming forging blanks and finished machined components routed through Plant P1 where machining surface finish affects functional fit, wear life, and downstream processing. The document supplements operational procedures and change notices; refer to ECN-2026-002, SOP-P1-L4-01, and SOP-P1-L4-02 for process setup, batch handling, and heat treat workflow.

Requirements table
| Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Evidence to record |
|---|---|---|
| Surface finish after final machining | Conforms to drawing surface finish callouts and functional fit for mating parts | Final inspection report with measured locations and inspector initials; include referenced drawing revision |
| Machine setup | Tools and machine parameters set per SOP-P1-L4-01 and SOP-P1-L4-02 | Setup checklist completed and retained with job traveler |
| Post-heat treat timing for quench | The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds. | Heat treat batch log indicating furnace ID, timer start/stop, and operator signature |
| Visual surface integrity | No visible machining tears, deep gouges, or foreign material embedded in critical surfaces | Visual inspection record and photographs where nonconformances are observed |
| Debris removal prior to inspection | Component clean and free of cutting fluids and chips per SOP-P1-L4-02 | Cleaning verification on inspection form |

Inspection method
Background and rationale
Surface finish is a primary determinant of part function where contact, sealing, or bearing surfaces are employed. Machining steps can introduce fine irregularities, tool marks, or embedded debris that compromise assembly and performance. This inspection method describes procedures to verify finish and to capture timing with the heat treat step, since surface characteristics can change when parts are quenched or otherwise processed thermally.

Preparation
- Confirm the job traveler and referenced drawing are present. Cross-reference with SOP-P1-L4-01 for machine set up and SOP-P1-L4-02 for cleaning and handling.
- Verify heat treat records for the lot processed through EQ-P1-L4-HT03. Ensure the quench delay timing is recorded as required.

Measurement points and instrumentation
- Identify critical surfaces as called out on the drawing. When no explicit callout exists, inspect functional mating surfaces and visible bearing interfaces.
- Use calibrated surface finish measuring instruments and visual aids as specified in SOP-P1-L4-01. Calibration status must be current and recorded.

Procedure
- Clean the part in accordance with SOP-P1-L4-02 before any measurement.
- Measure surface finish at the designated locations. Record instrument used and reading for each point.
- For batches processed in the furnace identified as EQ-P1-L4-HT03, verify the quench delay in the heat treat batch log. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds. Record the logged time next to inspection measurements to maintain traceability between thermal processing and surface condition.
- Document any surface anomalies with high-resolution photographs and annotate the location on the drawing or a copy of the inspection form.
- Complete the final inspection report, sign, and attach the heat treat batch log extract.

Examples and interpretation
- Example: If a mating surface shows higher than expected roughness readings but the heat treat batch log indicates a quench delay within the required maximum for EQ-P1-L4-HT03, the deviation is likely machining related. Follow nonconformance handling below.
- Example: If roughness readings are acceptable but visual inspection reveals embedded debris, the cause may be inadequate cleaning post-machining. Recleaning and reinspection are required per SOP-P1-L4-02 and records must show corrective action.
- Record linkage: For any condition that may relate to thermal processing, include the EQ-P1-L4-HT03 identifier and the quench delay value exactly as logged to facilitate later root cause analysis.

Records to keep
- Final inspection report with surface finish readings and annotated drawing.
- Heat treat batch log extract showing furnace ID and quench delay for EQ-P1-L4-HT03.
- Machine setup checklist per SOP-P1-L4-01.
- Cleaning verification per SOP-P1-L4-02.
- Photographic evidence of any nonconformance.
All records shall be retained in the document control system under the job traveler and referenced by job number and lot for traceability.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and containment
- Any part that fails to meet the acceptance criteria in the requirements table shall be segregated and clearly labeled until disposition.
- For conditions possibly linked to heat treat timing, include the EQ-P1-L4-HT03 batch log and the recorded quench delay. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds; verify compliance before further disposition.

Disposition options
- Rework: If deviation is limited to machinable defects (for example, tool marks beyond acceptable limits), machine rework is permitted if rework does not affect material integrity or functional dimensions. Re-inspect and record results.
- Repair: For surface defects that can be corrected by controlled processes defined in SOP-P1-L4-02, follow repair procedure and document operator and inspection approval.
- Reject: If defects compromise function or safety and cannot be corrected without altering the part beyond allowed limits, move to reject and document per plant rejection workflow.

Root cause and corrective action
- Initiate an investigation for recurring defects or any case where the quench delay log for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 shows a value exceeding the specified maximum. Reference ECN-2026-002 when proposed process changes are required.
- Document root cause analysis and corrective actions. Update SOP-P1-L4-01 and SOP-P1-L4-02 only after authorization and align with ECN-2026-002 as needed.

Review and approval
- Inspectors, heat treat operators, and process engineers shall review combined inspection and heat treat records for conformity. Any change to acceptance criteria or measurement methods must be controlled through ECN-2026-002.

End of document.
